INSIGHTS
Investor Presentation · Series A · 2026

The next revolutionary dataset: human behavior in game worlds.

We pay gamers in real prizes to record how they play, then license that consented, high-fidelity behavioral data to the AI labs building world models.

Insights — Series A
INSIGHTS
The problem

Frontier AI is starved of high-fidelity, ground-truth human behavior.

Synthetic plateaus

Simulated data can't reproduce authentic human decision-making — the highest-value signal for training.

Scraped falls short

Twitch and YouTube footage is low-fidelity and stripped of the inputs and metadata that make data useful.

No action signal

Public video is inferred, not recorded — it lacks the timestamped keystroke and mouse inputs that are ground truth.

Insights — Series A
INSIGHTS
Why now

The next wave of AI is world models for embodied intelligence.

And gameplay is its single richest source of training data: diverse, ground-truth, and multimodal, at a scale nothing else can match. We supply that pre-training data to every lab, not just one.

PROOF POINT
8 min

General Intuition pre-trained a model on millions of hours of gameplay, then powered a quadrupedal robot after just eight minutes of real-world fine-tuning.

TECHCRUNCH · JULY 2026

The opportunity

What this data will build.

World models are the foundation for machines that perceive, predict, and act in the physical world. Human gameplay is the pre-training substrate for all of it.

Humanoid robots

General-purpose robots that learn tasks from real human behaviour.

Autonomous vehicles

Driving policies grounded in genuine human decision-making.

AI agents

Agents that plan and act inside complex digital environments.

Robotics & manipulation

Dexterous control learned from millions of decision examples.

Drones & navigation

Spatial reasoning and route-planning in rich 3D worlds.

Game & simulation AI

Believable NPCs and simulated humans for training and testing.

Industrial automation

Embodied systems for warehouses, factories, and logistics.

Spatial & AR assistants

Assistants that understand and reason about physical context.

Insights — Series A
INSIGHTS
The acquisition engine

The Shards Program is just getting started.

Today it's rewards for playing. Next it becomes a living, gamified economy — a reason for millions to keep recording, at a fraction of paid-acquisition cost.

An online treasure hunt

Rare colored Shards, random loot drops, and mystery chests hidden across game worlds turn everyday play into a daily hunt.

Sponsored events & drops

Brands and studios fund tournaments, seasonal quests, and prize pools — a second revenue line that subsidizes acquisition.

A self-funding economy

Data revenue and sponsorships fund the prize pool — so growth compounds without burning capital on ads.

More than a rewards program: a viral, self-funding growth loop that makes Insights the cheapest place in the world to acquire engaged gamers — and the richest place to capture their behaviour.
Insights — Series A
INSIGHTS
Business model

Two revenue streams, one engine.

The free consumer app pays for its own growth through advertising, while the data business monetizes the behaviour it captures at high margin.

Primary · high margin

Data licensing

We license consented, labeled gameplay datasets to AI labs on a per-hour basis — from $100K proof-of-concepts to $5–60M/yr dedicated pipelines.

$5.0M active deal · 12× labs in pipeline
Funds acquisition

Advertising

The free app monetizes its huge, engaged player base through in-app advertising, generating ~$0.25 per user each month — revenue that scales with every download and funds the prizes that acquire the next players.

Insights — Series A
INSIGHTS
The moat

Almost no one can produce this data at scale.

This dataset can't be scraped or bought off a shelf. Producing it requires three things almost no one has together — and we are one of the very few sources on earth doing it at scale today.

A consenting community

A large, engaged, opted-in global player base that keeps generating fresh behaviour every day — the hardest piece to build.

Purpose-built capture

Synced video, timestamped inputs, and audio at broadcast quality — zero FPS drop, ban-safe, and impossible to reconstruct from public video.

Rights & provenance

Per-player consent and full chain-of-custody, so every dataset is clean, licensable, and defensible for the labs that buy it.

Competitors are flat at ~20K hours and 50 titles. We're at 540K hours across 415 titles and compounding — the flywheel widens the gap every single day.
